title: `new` on an enum passes the checker.
text: `new M();` for `enum M { A }` passes the checker and stops at `E0901` (`nvs-codegen does not lower a reference to class M`). `M $m = new M();` is `E0401` with the message "expected `M`, found `M`", which names the same type twice. An enum has no constructor and no object form (`rule:enums/no-class-machinery`), so `new` on one is a diagnostic of its own. It closes when `new` naming an enum is a single checker error that says an enum case is written `M::Case`, with a conformance case for both forms.
